title: Taking a call
purpose: How an advisor handles a first call; teaches exactly what the call scorecard checks, in the best closer's voice.
facts: The eight scorecard checks with their weights (calls design): greeting 1, name and number 2, need discovery 2, price with next step 2, offered time 3, asked for booking 3, recap 1, objection 2.
Example lines are the level-2 lines of the calls design.
Checks 5 and 6 carry the most weight; a call that ends on the price fails both.
Checks do not apply when the customer is known, names a time, or raises no doubt.
Automatic fails: wrong promise, dropped customer, promised call back not kept.
Inspection price in the example line is the brake inspection menu price.
Slot 6's weakest check is the objection (S4); slot 7's two wrong promises (S8, S12) are the first automatic fail.
The approved team note "offer a time before the price on a first call" is about order and is deliberately not on this page; the page says "a price with a next step attached".

rows.What: Greeting with our name and yours

rows.What it sounds like: "And the best number for you? ...0142, perfect."

rows.What: Find out what is going on. The car, and one question more than you need
rows.What it sounds like: "How long has it been doing that? Does it change when you brake?"

rows.What: A price with a next step attached
rows.What it sounds like: "It is $49.95 for the inspection, and I could get you in Friday at eight."

rows.What: Offer a time. Two of them
Ask for the booking and take it
rows.What it sounds like: "I have you down for Friday at eight. Ask for Maya."

rows.What: Recap: day, time, which shop, what we are doing
rows.What it sounds like: "Friday at eight, East Main Street, front brakes inspected."

rows.What: Answer the doubt, if there is one
rows.What it sounds like: "Did somebody quote it lower? Here is what is in that number."

list_items.section: The three ways to fail a call outright
list_items.item: A wrong promise. A price that is not on the price list. "Same day" before parts and a technician are confirmed: what you may promise. If you do not know, say "let me check and call you back by two" and call back by two.

list_items.section: The three ways to fail a call outright
list_items.item: Dropping the customer. A hold that never comes back, a transfer to nobody, a hang-up.

list_items.section: The three ways to fail a call outright
list_items.item: A call back you promised and did not make.
Smile before you pick up. They hear it.
The first price a caller asks for is not their real question. Their real question is "can I trust you with my car". Answer that one by asking about the car.
Never price "brakes" without the car. Pads on a Corolla and pads on an F-250 are different jobs.
When you offer two times, stop talking. Let them pick.
If they say "I will call you back", ask "would it help if I held Friday at eight for you until tomorrow noon?" Then hold it.
If the call is about a car that is already here, start with their name and end with what happens next and when.

new_facts: Holding a slot "until tomorrow noon" for an undecided caller (habit, no data footprint).
